answer: Coordination Kernel Pricing. Each agent action carries a fee set by the number of distinct identities whose signatures must co-sign within a fixed window; the kernel computes this from recent co-signature graphs and charges the full coordination cost to the initiator. An attacker cannot forge cheap breadth because adding identities multiplies the required co-signatures and the fee. Each extra identity costs the attacker a full coordination round plus its share of the marble-like fixed compute budget, making N identities cost N² work.
